questions.problem:
$$ \{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}=2x(1-x)-xy \\ {y}^{′}=-2y+4xy\end{aligned} $$ Consider the Lotka-Volterra model with carrying capacity above, where $x=x(t)$ represents the prey and $y=y(t)$ represents the predators. Select the correct options in the reasoning below. $\,$ Evaluating the Jacobian of the system at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[0.5,\,1]^{T},$ we get
$J({x}^{∗})=\,\,$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}} $\,.$
{{field-3}} {{field-4}}
$\,$ The eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix are {{field-5}}. $\,$ Therefore, the equilibrium at ${x}^{∗}$ is {{field-6}}{{field-7}}.
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote ${f}_{1}(x,y)=2x(1-x)-xy$ and ${f}_{2}(x,y)=-2y+4xy.$

Now, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x(1-x)-xy)=2-4x-y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x(1-x)-xy)=-x \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-2y+4xy)=4y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-2y+4xy)=-2+4x\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the Jacobian matrix is

$$
J=[\begin{aligned}2-4x-y & -x \\ 4y & -2+4x\end{aligned}].
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[\begin{aligned}0.5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ to get

$$
J({x}^{∗})=[\begin{aligned}2-4(0.5)-(1) & -(0.5) \\ 4(1) & -2+4(0.5)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -0.5 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix, we write down the characteristic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & -0.5 \\ 4 & -\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )(-\lambda )-4\cdot (-0.5) & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+\lambda +2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation, we get the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1,2}=-0.5\pm 0.5\sqrt{7}\,\text{i}.$ Since the eigenvalues are complex with negative real parts, our equilibrium is $\text{an asymptotically stable}$ $\text{spiral sink}.$

Select the correct options in the reasoning below. $\,$ Evaluating the Jacobian of the system at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[0,\,0]^{T},$ we get
$J({x}^{∗})=\,\,$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}} $\,.$

questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote ${f}_{1}(x,y)=2x(1-4x)-xy$ and ${f}_{2}(x,y)=-2y+4xy.$

Now, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x(1-4x)-xy)=2-16x-y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x(1-4x)-xy)=-x \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-2y+4xy)=4y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-2y+4xy)=-2+4x\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the Jacobian matrix is

$$
J=[\begin{aligned}2-16x-y & -x \\ 4y & -2+4x\end{aligned}].
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ to get

$$
J({x}^{∗})=[\begin{aligned}2-16(0)-(0) & -(0) \\ 4(0) & -2+4(0)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

The eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=2\text{ and }{\lambda }_{2}=-2.$ Since the eigenvalues are real with opposite signs, our equilibrium is $\text{an unstable}$ $\text{saddle}.$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}=2x(1-0.1x)-xy \\ {y}^{′}=-3y+xy\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the Lotka-Volterra model with carrying capacity above, where $x=x(t)$ represents the prey and $y=y(t)$ represents the predators. The equilibria of the model are the following:

$(0,0),\,(${{field-1}}$,0),\,(${{field-2}}$,${{field-3}}$)$
questions.worked_solution:
The equilibrium (fixed) points of a system ${x}^{′}(t)=f(x,y)$ are the points for which $f(x,y)=0.$ So, we get the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x(1-0.1x)-xy=0 \\ -3y+xy=0\end{aligned}
$$

Factoring the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-3y+xy & =0 \\ y(-3+x) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $y=0$ or $x=3.$ We consider both cases separately.

- If $y=0,$ substituting it into the first equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2x(1-0.1x)-x(0) & =0 \\ 2x(0.1x-1) & =0 \\ x & =0,\,10.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the first two equilibria are $(0,0)$ and $(10,0).$

- If $x=3,$ substituting it into the first equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2(3)(1-0.1(3))-(3)y & =0 \\ 4.2-3y & =0 \\ y & =1.4.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, another equilibrium is $(3,1.4).$

Therefore, the equilibria of the model are

$$
(0,0),\,(10,0),\,(3,1.4).
$$
